synopsis: South Africa Regulation 8.10 requires automatic detection and warning, followed by retardation to a safe speed if the operator does not act, then automatic braking with fail-to-safe behaviour; its test objects include pedestrians and other diesel trackless mobile machines [f2441, f2439, f11182]. The reviewed passages provide no universal distance or speed threshold, stopping-margin value or deceleration curve, consistent with the glossary's statement that the regulation supplies no numerical requirements [f2440, f2611, f2442, f15637]. The Minerals Council describes the regulation as stating what must be done rather than how, and its MOSH programme developed surface collision-prevention performance requirements, a verification regime and independent test specifications to fill that engineering gap [f10458, f15638]. Expert-opinion commentary reports suspension in 2015 because technology was unavailable, while a separate fact records commencement on 21 December 2022 [f10457, f11183, f11184]. Interoperability with collision systems already deployed at customer sites, including legally mandated systems, remains a stated concern [f10513].
